item.title: Oman Makes Premarital Medical Screening Mandatory
item.description: Oman has made premarital medical screening mandatory for couples planning to marry, in a move aimed at early detection of hereditary blood disorders and infectious diseases and at providing medical counselling before marriage, the Ministry of Health said. The ministry said the measure is designed to help reduce the transmission of certain genetic and communicable diseases, prevent avoidable health conditions in children and ease the social, psychological and financial burden on families. item.description: Cold weather is set to ease gradually across the Arab Gulf region and wider Arabian Peninsula as the final phase of winter, traditionally known as the “Scorpions season”, begins on February 6 and continues until March 18, according to an Emirati astronomy expert. item.title: Saudi Arabia: Madinah Buses To Operate Shuttle Service For Worshipers In Ramadan
item.description: Madinah Region Development Authority announced the launch of a shuttle bus service at various stations during the upcoming holy month of Ramadan to facilitate the movement of worshipers and visitors to and from the Prophet’s Mosque and Quba Mosque. The authority said the service aims to enhance the experience of worshipers and visitors, reduce congestion around places of worship during the holy month, and provide organized transportation that ensures the comfort and safety of all.

item.title: Bahrain: Labour Court Awards Manager More Than BD 33,000 For Unpaid Wages And Benefits
item.description: The First High Labor Court has ordered a company to pay a manager more than BD 33,000 in compensation for delayed wages, annual leave allowance, end-of-service benefits, and legal interest. Under the ruling, the court ordered the company to pay BD 21,658 in unpaid wages, along with legal interest calculated at 6% annually for wages delayed for up to six months from the date they became due. item.title: Bahrain: Drugs Found Hidden In Dried Fish
item.description: A man and woman were intercepted at Bahrain International Airport after customs officers became suspicious of their suitcases. Using a sophisticated method to conceal narcotics among dried fish and shrimp, the defendants attempted to pass through customs.
